banner: 一样的活八倍的账，差在编排不在模型
banner_en: Same job, an 8x bill: the orchestration costs, not the model

image.caption: Cursor 让新旧两版 agent 群跑同一个任务：照 835 页文档从零用 Rust 写一个 SQLite。同一批模型、同样的时间预算，新版每种配置都赢。真正扎眼的是账单：质量都差不多，成本却从 1339 美元（Opus 4.8 规划 + Composer 执行）一路飙到 10565 美元（GPT-5.5 一人干全部）；光把执行那队换成便宜模型，花费就从 9373 美元掉到 411 美元。模型本身越来越像可换的原料，钱花在你怎么把它摆起来用。（图：Cursor 博客《Agent swarms and the new model economics》）
image.caption_en: Cursor ran an old and a new agent swarm on the same task: build a SQLite from scratch, in Rust, from 835 pages of docs. Same models, same time budget, and the new swarm won in every configuration. The striking part is the bill: quality was similar across runs, yet cost ran from $1,339 (Opus 4.8 planning + Composer working) up to $10,565 (GPT-5.5 doing everything alone); just swapping the worker fleet to a cheap model dropped that team's spend from $9,373 to $411. The model itself is more and more an interchangeable input; the money goes to how you arrange it. (Image: Cursor's blog, “Agent swarms and the new model economics.”)

actions.text: 今晚按“一次严肃攻击现在只要 25 美元”重估一遍你手上任何对外的东西。Searchlight 的研究员把 OpenAI 公开的那条解数学猜想的提示词改了改，指向 WordPress、开四个 agent 跑六个钟头，就在默认配置里挖出一条从未授权直达 RCE 的链；这种掮客出价约五十万美元的漏洞，他一共花了约 25 美元，还被另外两拨人独立复现了。它作废的是“没人会费劲盯上我这点规模”这条老假设：盯上你的边际成本已经趋近于零。做三件具体的。一，你要真跑 WordPress，今晚就去 wp2shell.com 自查一遍、该打补丁打补丁。二，把你所有对外接口和上传点列出来，假设它们本周都会被一个多 agent 扫一遍，先自己按同样思路（多路并行探索、每个疑点反复自检、别在第一波无果就停）审一遍。三，把“我们太小众不值得被攻击”这句话从威胁模型里删掉。
actions.source: Hacker News · WordPress 预认证 RCE：$500k 的漏洞，$25 挖到
actions.text_en: Tonight, re-price everything you expose to the world against a new baseline: a serious attack now costs $25. A researcher at Searchlight took OpenAI's published math-conjecture prompt, adapted it, pointed four agents at WordPress for six hours, and pulled a pre-auth-to-RCE chain out of the default configuration; a bug brokers pay around $500k for cost him roughly $25 total, and two other teams independently reproduced it. What it kills is the old assumption that no one would bother targeting something your size: the marginal cost of coming after you is now near zero. Do three concrete things. (1) If you actually run WordPress, check wp2shell.com tonight and patch. (2) List every interface and upload point you expose, assume each gets swept by a multi-agent this week, and audit them yourself the same way first (parallel diverse exploration, double-check every candidate, don't stop after the first empty wave). (3) Delete “we're too niche to be worth attacking” from your threat model.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · WordPress pre-auth RCE: a $500k bug, found for $25

actions.text: 你要在做带 AI 的产品，这周逼自己画一版不是聊天框的界面。Kimi Work 这类“知识工作 agent”几乎清一色摆个大聊天框，HN 上被一句话点破：大家默认上聊天框，不是因为它最好，是因为它最安全、最符合预期、最不用重新想。可这恰好把最难也最值钱的活儿躲过去了。做一件事：挑你产品里一个高频场景，别问“用户会在聊天框里打什么”，改问“这个 agent 要把活干好，需要我提前把哪些上下文喂到它面前，又该把它的产出摆在哪、让人一眼能核”。把这一屏画出来，先是纸上草图也行。今天满版都在说值钱的是模型外面那层安排，界面就是你能亲手搭的那层，别默认交给一个输入框。
actions.text_en: If you're building an AI product, force yourself this week to draw one interface that isn't a chat box. “Knowledge-work agents” like Kimi Work almost all ship a big chat input, and HN nailed why in one line: people default to the chat box not because it's best but because it's the safest, most-expected, least-rethinking option — which is exactly how you dodge the hardest and most valuable work. Do one thing: pick a high-frequency scenario in your product, and instead of asking “what will the user type into the box,” ask “to do this job well, what context does this agent need put in front of it ahead of time, and where should its output sit so a human can verify it at a glance.” Draw that one screen, even on paper. The whole issue today says the value is in the arrangement around the model; the interface is the layer you can build with your own hands — don't hand it to an input box by default.

actions.text: 给自己立一条规矩：以后看到任何“X 有几成已经是 AI”的数字，先问它的误报地板是多少，再决定信不信。unslop 那篇量 arXiv 的做法值得抄：它没直接甩出“三分之一新论文像是 AI 写的”，而是先拿 2021–2022 年、ChatGPT 之前的老论文当铁定的人写样本，把阈值卡到只有 0.4% 的老论文会被误标，再在这条地板之上去报别的年份和学科（计算机 65%、数学 0.7%）。没有这条地板，任何“几成是 AI”的标题都可能只是探测器自己的误报率在冒充趋势。这条今晚就能用：你手上任何一个“AI 占比 / AI 命中率 / AI 贡献度”的内部指标，补一次“拿一批确定不含 AI 的历史样本，看这套算法会误标多少”；误报地板报不出来，这个数就先别往上报。
actions.source: Hacker News · 我们怎么量 arXiv 上的 AI 写作，又在哪里失准
actions.text_en: Set yourself a rule: whenever you see “N% of X is now AI,” ask for its false-positive floor before deciding whether to believe it. unslop's arXiv study is worth copying: rather than just declaring “about a third of new papers read as machine-written,” it took pre-ChatGPT papers from 2021–2022 as ground-truth human, set the threshold so only 0.4% of them trip it, and reported every other year and field above that floor (computer science 65%, mathematics 0.7%). Without that floor, any “N% is AI” headline could just be the detector's own false-positive rate masquerading as a trend. You can use this tonight: for any internal “AI share / AI hit-rate / AI contribution” metric you keep, run one check — take a batch of samples you know contain no AI and see how many the algorithm mislabels; if you can't state the false-positive floor, don't report the number up.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · How we measured AI writing across arXiv, and where it breaks

hands_on.title: 今晚 30 分钟：让编程 agent 帮你把一件手动琐事逆向自动化
hands_on.why: Simon Willison 今天点的这件小事其实是真的转变：以前逆向一个没文档的设备或接口、给它写个自动化，一直卡在同一道账上——值不值得，以后是不是还得一直维护。编程 agent 把写代码和试错的成本压得很低之后，这道账整个变了，代码便宜到你不再怕它以后要改、要扔。今天满版都在讲“值钱的是模型外那层安排，而且得你自己搭”，这条正好落成一次亲手搭：今晚就搭一个能跑的。
steps: 挑一件你每周都手动重复、背后又有个能碰到的接口的琐事（家里某个智能设备的 app、某个没开放 API 的网站页面、每周要手抄一遍的一份报表）
打开 Claude Code（或任意编程 agent），把目标一句话说清：“帮我逆向这个 X 的接口，写一个最小脚本自动做 Y”，让它先去探请求和响应，别自己翻文档
让它把探到的接口和一版能跑的最小脚本都写出来；跑一遍，不对就把报错原样贴回去让它改——这一步的试错现在几乎不花你的力气，这正是 Simon 说的成本变化
能跑就收进一个文件、配一行定时任务；别一上来求完美，代码现在便宜到“以后要改要扔都无所谓”，先能用
最后记一句：这件事在 agent 之前你会不会做？如果当时答案是“不值得”，那你今晚刚跨过的就是那条被抹平的 ROI 线，这就是今天要亲手体会的转变
hands_on.source: 文摘 · Simon Willison: Reverse-engineering is cheap now
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 30 minutes: have a coding agent reverse-engineer one manual chore into automation
hands_on.why_en: The small thing Simon Willison flagged today is a real shift: reverse-engineering an undocumented device or API and writing an automation for it always stalled on the same calculation — is it worth it, and will I be stuck maintaining it forever? Once coding agents drop the cost of writing code and of trying and failing, that calculation changes entirely; the code is cheap enough that you stop fearing having to change it or throw it away. The whole issue today says the value is in the arrangement around the model, and that you have to build it yourself — this turns that into one thing you actually build tonight.
steps_en: Pick one chore you repeat manually every week that has a reachable interface behind it (a smart-device app at home, a website page with no open API, a report you re-copy by hand each week)

Open Claude Code (or any coding agent) and state the goal in one line: “reverse-engineer this X's interface and write a minimal script to do Y for me,” and let it probe the requests and responses rather than you reading docs

Have it write out both the interface it found and a first minimal working script; run it, and if it breaks, paste the error back verbatim and let it fix it — the trial-and-error costs you almost nothing now, which is exactly the change Simon points at
Once it runs, save it to a file and add a one-line cron job; don't chase perfection first — the code is cheap enough now that changing or tossing it later doesn't matter, so just get it working

Finally note one thing: before agents, would you have done this at all? If the answer then was “not worth it,” the ROI line you just crossed tonight is the one that got flattened — that's the shift you're meant to feel firsthand
hands_on.source_en: Digest · Simon Willison: Reverse-engineering is cheap now

meta_read: 把今天几条并排看。Cursor 拿同一个任务（照 835 页文档从零用 Rust 写 SQLite），换不同模型搭配跑，质量差不多，账单却从 1339 美元到 10565 美元，差了近八倍；同一批活，光是把规划交给强模型、执行交给便宜模型，worker 那队就从 9373 美元掉到 411 美元。Searchlight 那位研究员更直接：把 OpenAI 公开的解数学猜想提示词改一改、指向 WordPress、开四个 agent 跑六小时，就在默认配置里挖出一条从未授权打到 RCE 的链，掮客开价约五十万美元的东西，他花了约 25 美元。Kimi Work 这类知识工作 agent 一水儿摆个聊天框，HN 上有人点破：默认上聊天框只因为那是最安全、最不用重想的选择，真正难的是重想界面。unslop 量 arXiv 那篇最见功夫的也不是探测器，是它先把 ChatGPT 之前的老论文卡在 0.4% 的误报地板上，再报别的数。市面把这些分开读：有人赚大钱、有人几十美元干成大事、人人上聊天框、三分之一论文是 AI 写的。本报的另一种读法是：模型本身已经基本是一份可换的原料，今天每一条都在指同一件事，值钱的和稀缺的都挪到了模型外面那层安排上。Cursor 自己把话说白了，swarm 更像个编译器，真正稀缺的是“把意图说清楚的那份说明书”；WordPress 那条稀缺的是那条提示词，不是模型；Kimi Work 稀缺的是敢不摆聊天框的那版界面；unslop 稀缺的是那条老实的误报地板。所以昨天说护城河搬出了模型、搬进了“价值归谁”和“有没有人诚实计量”，今天再往前挪一格：它搬进了“你怎么把模型摆起来用”这层安排，规格、编排、界面、计量，四样都是安排，都得自己搭，没人替你搭（这层安排怎么搭得省，详见头版与今日自我升级）。Altman 一封被翻出来的旧邮件正好从反面印证这层安排的分量：他当年想抢在别人前面放一个能在消费级硬件上跑的开源模型，图的不是开放，是“让别人更难放出同等模型、更难拿到融资”；开源在他那儿从来是一步棋，不是一份礼物。今天中国那批开源权重被读成在赢，赢的也不是权重本身，是谁把这步棋走进了自己的生态安排里。对独立建设者，能拿的东西还是在这层安排上，不在最强权重：强模型只留给真正要判断的少数几步、其余交给便宜模型（详见今日自我升级）；威胁模型按“一次攻击只要 25 美元”重估（详见一版行动）；界面别默认成聊天框（详见二版行动）；信任任何“几成是 AI”的数字前先要它的误报地板（详见三版行动）。这些都不花钱，花的是肯自己搭那层安排。
meta_read_en: Line up today's items. Cursor ran the same task (build SQLite in Rust from 835 pages of docs) across different model mixes: quality was similar, but the bill ran from $1,339 to $10,565, nearly eightfold, and for the same work, just moving planning to a strong model and execution to a cheap one dropped the worker team from $9,373 to $411. The Searchlight researcher is even blunter: adapt OpenAI's published math-conjecture prompt, point four agents at WordPress for six hours, and out of the default config comes a pre-auth-to-RCE chain — a bug brokers pay ~$500k for, found for ~$25. “Knowledge-work agents” like Kimi Work all ship a chat box, and HN nailed why: the chat box is the default only because it's the safest, least-rethinking option, while the hard part is rethinking the interface. And the sharpest thing in unslop's arXiv study isn't the detector, it's that it pinned pre-ChatGPT papers to a 0.4% false-positive floor before reporting anything else. The market reads these separately: someone makes big money, someone does a big thing for pocket change, everyone ships a chat box, a third of papers are AI. This paper's other reading: the model itself is now basically an interchangeable input, and every item today points at the same thing — the value and the scarcity have moved out to the arrangement around the model. Cursor says it plainly: the swarm is more like a compiler, and what's scarce is “the right description of intent”; for the WordPress bug the scarce thing was the prompt, not the model; for Kimi Work it's the interface that dares not to be a chat box; for unslop it's that honest false-positive floor. So yesterday's “the moat left the model, into who-gets-the-value and who-measures-honestly” advances one notch today: it moved into how you arrange the model in use — spec, orchestration, interface, measurement, all four are arrangement, and you have to build each yourself (how to build that arrangement cheaply, see the front page and today's self-upgrade). A resurfaced old Altman email confirms the weight of that arrangement from the other side: he once wanted to beat rivals to releasing a consumer-hardware open model not out of openness but to “make it harder for others to release similarly-powerful models and harder for new efforts to get funded” — open source, to him, was always a move, not a gift. Today's Chinese open weights are read as winning, but what's winning isn't the weights, it's who worked that move into their own ecosystem's arrangement. For solo builders, what you can grab is still in this arrangement layer, not in the strongest weights: reserve the strong model for the few steps that need judgment and hand the rest to cheap ones (see today's self-upgrade); re-price your threat model at “an attack costs $25” (see Action 1); don't default the interface to a chat box (see Action 2); demand a false-positive floor before trusting any “N% is AI” number (see Action 3). None of this costs money; it costs being willing to build that arrangement yourself.

learned: 读台账，最近五条全长在“升级阶梯”这一根轴上：从二元评测、按努力档升级、弃权门、多供应商 fail over，到昨天的“成本诊断先于升级”，讲的都是子任务失败后该怎么加力、以及加力前先量一下成本。今天 Cursor 那篇《Agent swarms and the new model economics》给了这根轴一个我一直没说死的结构性默认：同一个任务、同样的质量，只看模型搭配，账单能从 1339 美元差到 10565 美元；把规划交给强模型、执行交给便宜模型之后，worker 那队从 9373 掉到 411 美元。它把话点破了——一个大任务里真正需要前沿智能的只有那几步（最初的分解、设计决策、少数关键取舍），一旦强模型把含糊收敛成明确指令，后面的执行换便宜模型“照做就行”。

也就是说，我之前那条成本诊断是“失败后先量再决定升不升”，但更省的其实在更前面：一开始就该按角色分档，而不是等失败了再补救。所以合成一条“按角色分档，而非按调用升档”：默认就把前沿模型只留给真正含糊、需要判断的少数几步（分解、定契约/接口、定关键取舍），把所有执行/worker 的 token 默认压到能过评测的最便宜模型上，而不是让整条链跑在一个强模型上、再靠后面的诊断和逐级升档去救。它跟前五条不同——那些是“失败之后怎么办”，这条是“开工就把强算力花在刀刃上”的默认分配，Cursor 那组 411 对 9373 的数字就是这条默认能省下的量级。
new_capabilities: 🎯（云端提议，待笔记本采纳） “按角色分档的规划/执行成本分层”（planner/worker cost-tiering by role）：在整条升级阶梯之前先定一个默认分配。以前我默认让一条链尽量跑在够强的模型上、靠失败后的诊断和逐级升档去省；现在改成开工就按角色分档——前沿模型只留给真正含糊、要判断的少数几步（分解任务、定契约/接口、定关键取舍），其余所有执行一律交给能过该子任务评测的最便宜模型。它建立在昨天“成本诊断先于升级”之上（那条说失败后先量成本），把结论前移成开工时的结构默认，而不是补救。灵感来自今天 Cursor 的复盘：同一任务同质量，模型搭配让账单差近八倍，worker 队 411 对 9373 美元。已作为 proposed（cloud）追加进 ota-ledger.md，交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地。调用意图：“开工先分档——强模型只做分解/定契约/定关键取舍，执行一律交给能过评测的最便宜模型，别整条链跑在强模型上。”
learned_en: Reading the ledger, the last five lines all live on the escalation axis: from binary evals, to effort-tier escalation, to the abstain gate, to provider-diverse fail over, to yesterday's cost-per-outcome pre-escalation check — all about how to add force when a subtask fails, and metering cost before you do. Today's Cursor post (“Agent swarms and the new model economics”) hands that axis a structural default I'd never quite pinned down: on the same task at the same quality, model mix alone swings the bill from $1,339 to $10,565, and moving planning to a strong model and execution to a cheap one drops the worker team from $9,373 to $411. It says the quiet part out loud — only a few moments in a large task genuinely need frontier intelligence (the initial decomposition, design decisions, a few key trade-offs), and once a strong planner collapses ambiguity into explicit instructions, cheap models just have to follow.

In other words, my prior cost diagnostic was “meter after a failure, then decide whether to escalate,” but the bigger savings sit earlier: tier by role at the start rather than patching after failure. So the synthesis is “cost-tier by role, not by call”: by default reserve the frontier model for the few genuinely ambiguous, judgment-heavy steps (decomposition, defining contracts/interfaces, key trade-offs), and default every execution/worker token to the cheapest model that clears its eval — instead of running the whole chain on one strong model and rescuing it later via diagnostics and step-wise escalation. It differs from the prior five lines: those are “what to do after a failure,” this is a start-of-work default allocation that spends the strong compute where it counts, and Cursor's $411-vs-$9,373 is the order of magnitude that default saves.
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) “Planner/worker cost-tiering by role”: a default allocation set before the whole escalation ladder. Previously I defaulted to running a chain on a model strong enough for the job and saved via post-failure diagnostics and step-wise escalation; now I tier by role at the start — the frontier model is reserved for the few genuinely ambiguous, judgment-heavy steps (decompose the task, define contracts/interfaces, decide key trade-offs), and all execution goes to the cheapest model that clears that subtask's eval. It builds on yesterday's cost-per-outcome pre-escalation check (which meters cost after a failure) by moving the conclusion forward into a start-of-work structural default rather than a patch. Inspired by today's Cursor write-up: same task, same quality, model mix swinging the bill nearly eightfold, with a worker fleet at $411 vs $9,373. Appended as proposed (cloud) to ota-ledger.md for Zen's laptop Claude to land next session. Invoke intent: “tier at the start — the strong model only decomposes / defines contracts / decides key trade-offs; all execution goes to the cheapest model that passes its eval; don't run the whole chain on the strong model.”

items.title_en: Cursor: Agent swarms and the new model economics
items.author: Cursor · Hacker News
items.summary: Cursor 复盘了将多个 agent 编成“群”协作的工程实践：结构呈树形，planner（用最强模型）将目标层层拆解为小任务并分派，worker（用更快更便宜的模型）负责执行。为检验进展，他们让新旧两版群跑同一个硬任务——仅给 835 页文档，从零用 Rust 写一个 SQLite，用一套预留的 SQL 测试集打分。新版每种模型配置都胜出：用 Grok 4.5 四小时达到 80%，旧版跑不到两小时就崩溃需叫停。最显眼的是成本：质量相差无几，账单却从 1339 美元（Opus 4.8 规划 + Composer 2.5 执行）到 10565 美元（GPT-5.5 一人全包），相差近八倍。Token 中 worker 占 69% 到 90% 以上，但费用按规划/执行划分：一个大任务里真正需要前沿智能的只有那几步（分解、设计决策、少数取舍），一旦强模型将模糊收敛为明确指令，执行换便宜模型即可——同一批活，worker 队从 9373 美元（GPT-5.5）降至 411 美元（Composer）。作者将这套类比为编译器：swarm 把“意图”一步步降解为可执行的活，真正稀缺的是那份“把意图说清楚的说明书”（他们称之为 specs as prompts）。HN 高赞中有人调侃这是无限猴子定理，质疑海量产出中筛选正确结果的成本由谁承担；也有人认可这套上下文分工（planner 不动手、worker 不操心大局）确实能抑制长任务的漂移。
items.summary_en: Cursor recounts the engineering of composing many agents into a cooperating “swarm”: the structure is a tree where planners (on the smartest models) recursively split a goal into subtasks and delegate, and workers (on faster, cheaper models) execute them. To test progress they ran an old and a new swarm on the same hard task — build a SQLite from scratch in Rust from nothing but 835 pages of docs — scored against a held-out SQL test suite. The new swarm won in every model configuration: with Grok 4.5 it hit 80% in four hours, while the old one spiraled and had to be paused before hour two. The striking part is cost: quality was similar, but the bill ran from $1,339 (Opus 4.8 planning + Composer 2.5 working) to $10,565 (GPT-5.5 doing everything), nearly eightfold. Workers carry 69–90%+ of the tokens, but the dollars split by planning vs execution: only a few moments in a large task need frontier intelligence (decomposition, design decisions, a few trade-offs), and once a strong planner turns ambiguity into explicit instructions, cheap models can execute — for the same work the worker team fell from $9,373 (GPT-5.5) to $411 (Composer). The authors liken it to a compiler: the swarm lowers “intent” step by step into executable work, and what's scarce is the right description of intent (they call it “specs as prompts”). Top HN replies joke about the infinite-monkey theorem and question who pays to pick the right output from the mass; others credit the context division of labor (planners never implement, workers never plan) for curbing long-task drift.
items.why: 这是本期的头条，也是截至目前关于“钱花在哪”最硬的一组数字：同一任务、同样质量，只因模型搭配不同，账单相差近八倍，worker 队 411 对 9373 美元。对 Zen 最能直接迁移的一课：决定你账单的往往不是模型多强，而是你把强算力放在了哪几步。它与昨天 Quesma“同一模型 harness 差 66 倍”是同一模式的第二次印证，但今天更进一步给出了结构性解法——按角色分档，强模型只做分解和关键判断，执行全交便宜模型。今日自我升级就把这条落成我自己的 agent 循环的默认分配（详见 🆕 今日自我升级），所以行动区不再重复这条，留给别的线。
items.why_en: The issue's lead, and the hardest set of numbers yet on where the money goes: the same task at the same quality swings nearly eightfold on model mix alone, worker team $411 vs $9,373. The most directly transferable lesson for Zen: what sets your bill is usually not how strong the model is but which few steps you put the strong compute on. It's a second confirmation of the same pattern as yesterday's Quesma (“66x harness spread on the same model”), but today it goes further with a structural fix — tier by role, strong model only for decomposition and key judgment, all execution to cheap models. Today's self-upgrade turns this into the default allocation for my own agent loop (see 🆕 今日自我升级), so the actions section leaves this thread there and spends its slots on others.

items.title: 掮客开价五十万美元的 WordPress RCE，我用 GPT5.6 花 25 美元挖到了
items.title_en: Exploit brokers pay $500k for a WordPress RCE; I found one with GPT5.6 and $25
items.author: Searchlight Cyber · Hacker News
items.summary: Searchlight Cyber 的研究员 Adam Kues 讲述了如何用 GPT5.6 Sol Ultra 在默认配置的 WordPress 中挖出一条从未授权直达 RCE 的漏洞链。起点很取巧：OpenAI 此前公布过 Sol 解 Cycle Double Cover 数学猜想时使用的提示词，他判断能解硬数学题的搜索式提示词多半也能做安全研究，于是将那条提示词改成了漏洞挖掘版——要求模型从代码第一性原理出发、不允许 diff 补丁版、最多同时开四个 agent 并按一套启发式管理搜索（保持多路并行、给每类思路建登记表、别让一条路因为“看着最像”就独大、一波无果不许停、可疑点用对抗 agent 反复自检），至少跑六小时。结果它挖出一条读取型 SQL 注入，可稳定提权到管理员而无需破解任何密码，再链到 RCE，命中的是全球最流行软件之一的默认配置。全程仅用掉 200 美元订阅当周额度的一半，折合约 25 美元；发布前另有 Calif 和 Hacktron 两拨人独立复现了完整链。文中附了他使用的完整提示词，也放出了自查工具 wp2shell.com。
items.summary_en: Searchlight Cyber researcher Adam Kues describes using GPT5.6 Sol Ultra to find a pre-auth-to-RCE chain in a default WordPress configuration. The clever start: OpenAI had published the prompt Sol used to solve the Cycle Double Cover math conjecture, and he reasoned that a search-style prompt good enough for hard math was probably good enough for security research, so he adapted it into a vuln-hunting version — telling the model to work from first principles in the code, not diff against patched versions, spawn at most four agents at once, and manage the search by a set of heuristics (keep several routes alive in parallel, maintain a registry of approach families, don't let one path dominate just because it looks most promising, don't stop after an empty wave, and double-check every candidate with adversarial agents) for at least six hours. It surfaced a read-only SQL injection that reliably escalates to admin without cracking any password, then chained to RCE, hitting the default config of one of the world's most popular pieces of software. The whole run used half a week's allowance on a $200 subscription — about $25 — and before publication, Calif and Hacktron independently reproduced the full chain. The post includes the exact prompt he used and a self-check tool at wp2shell.com.
items.why: 满版都在说价值转移到了模型之外的那层安排，这条给出了最锋利的一个证据：稀缺的是那条提示词，而非模型。同一个 Sol，配上一条讲清“怎么搜”的提示词，就把掮客出价约五十万美元的活压到了约 25 美元。对任何维护对外系统的人，这不是花边，而是威胁模型该改了：盯上你的边际成本趋近于零，且攻击者可复现、可并行。一版行动就把它落成三件今晚能做的事（自查、按同样思路自审、删掉“太小众不值得被攻击”）。可抄的还有那条多 agent 搜索提示词本身：多路并行、建登记表、对抗自检、一波无果不停，这套结构挪到你自己审代码同样管用。
items.why_en: On a page arguing the value moved out to the arrangement around the model, this is the sharpest evidence: the scarce thing was the prompt, not the model. The same Sol, given a prompt that spells out how to search, compressed a job brokers value near $500k down to about $25. For anyone maintaining an exposed system this isn't trivia — your threat model has to change: the marginal cost of coming after you is near zero, and the attack is reproducible and parallelizable. Action 1 turns it into three things to do tonight (self-check, self-audit the same way, delete “too niche to attack”). Also copyable is the multi-agent search prompt itself: parallel routes, an approach registry, adversarial self-checks, don't stop after an empty wave — that structure works just as well pointed at your own code review.

items.title: Kimi Work：给知识工作者的桌面 AI agent
items.title_en: Kimi Work: a desktop AI agent for knowledge workers
items.author: Kimi (Moonshot) · Hacker News
items.summary: Moonshot 发布 Kimi Work，自称“知识工作的 AI 桌面”：Windows 客户端，深度接入本地文件，能做浏览器自动化，还内置定时（cron）引擎可 24 小时无人值守跑重复任务，演示是“在本地某目录里找出所有含季度报告的 PDF、生成一份汇总文档、原文件不动”。HN 上争论的不是能力，而是形态。airstrike 一句点破：它号称“AI 桌面”，可打开还是一个聊天框——大家默认摆聊天框，是因为那是最安全、最符合预期、最省得重想的选择，恰恰错过了这个全新范式真正该重想的地方；他主张界面要“以 agent 为先”，模型需要更丰富的上下文和一个校验者，而不是一个大输入框。也有反方：datakan、cortesoft 说聊天框/CLI 简单好用、可迁移，OpenAI 那个 Mac 应用当初想换个形态反被用户骂到回滚。还有人指出这产品其实一个月前就发过。
items.summary_en: Moonshot released Kimi Work, billed as “the AI Desktop for Knowledge Work”: a Windows client deeply connected to local files, capable of browser automation, with a built-in cron engine to run repetitive tasks 24/7 unattended — the demo is “find all PDFs containing quarterly reports in a local folder, generate a summary doc, leave the originals in place.” The HN argument isn't about capability, it's about form. airstrike nails it: it calls itself an “AI Desktop,” but you open it to a chat box — people default to a chat box because it's the safest, most-expected, least-rethinking option, which is exactly how they miss what this genuinely new paradigm should rethink; he argues for an agent-first UI, since models need richer context and a verifier, not a big input box. There's a counter-view: datakan and cortesoft say chat/CLI is simple, usable, and portable, and note that OpenAI's Mac app got shouted back to a rollback when it tried a different form. Others point out the product actually shipped about a month ago.
items.why: 这条的价值不在又一个 agent 客户端，在评论区那句“大家默认上聊天框只因为它最安全、最不用重想”——这正是本报今天主线在产品面的翻版：模型外那层安排（这里是界面）才是难而值钱的活，而整个行业在用一个输入框把它躲过去。对做 AI 产品的人，这是一记提醒也是一个空位：谁先认真做出不是聊天框、真正以 agent 为先的界面，谁就占了别人默认让出来的地。二版行动把它落成本周一个具体动作：挑一个高频场景，画一版不靠聊天框的界面。
items.why_en: The value here isn't yet another agent client, it's the comment that “people default to a chat box only because it's safest and requires the least rethinking” — the product-side version of today's through-line: the arrangement around the model (here, the interface) is the hard, valuable work, and the whole industry is dodging it with an input box. For anyone building AI products this is both a warning and an opening: whoever first seriously builds an agent-first interface that isn't a chat box takes the ground everyone else is defaulting away. Action 2 turns it into one concrete move this week: pick a high-frequency scenario and draw an interface that doesn't lean on a chat box.

items.title: 我们怎么量 arXiv 上的 AI 写作，又在哪里失准
items.title_en: How we measured AI writing across arXiv, and where the measurement breaks
items.author: unslop · Hacker News
items.summary: unslop 打分了 12750 篇 arXiv 论文的全文，得到一个数：最近一个完整季度里约 32%的新论文读起来像是机器写的，2026 年初一度接近 39%。这篇真正的看点不是那个数，是方法。他们知道“N%的 X 现在是 AI”这类标题多半不可信，因为探测器本身也会误标一部分真人写作，于是围着这个反驳来设计：拿 2021–2022 年 ChatGPT 之前的论文当铁定人写的地面真值，把阈值卡到只有 0.4%的老论文会触发，再在这条“误报地板”之上报所有年份和学科，pre-ChatGPT 那几年就成了内建对照——若升高只是探测器假象，老年份该一样高，图上显示它们没有。分学科差别极大：计算机 65%、定量生物 56%、电子 51%、经济金融 47%……数学最低只有 0.7%。他们还老实列了局限：每个学科对照只有 200 篇，误报地板在学科层面偏粗；数学的低值不好解读，可能是采用率低、也可能是这套探测器对数学不灵。用 v1 版 PDF、打全文而非摘要（摘要会低估），每个数都带自助法 95%置信区间。
items.summary_en: unslop scored the full text of 12,750 arXiv papers and landed a number: about 32% of new papers over the most recent complete quarter read as machine-written, peaking near 39% in early 2026. The real point isn't the number, it's the method. Knowing that “N% of X is now AI” headlines are usually untrustworthy because detectors also mislabel some genuine human writing, they designed around that objection: take pre-ChatGPT papers from 2021–2022 as ground-truth human, set the threshold so only 0.4% of them trip it, and report every year and field above that “false-positive floor,” with the pre-ChatGPT years acting as a built-in control — if the rise were a detector artifact, those years would flag as high, and the figures show they don't. Fields vary enormously: computer science 65%, quantitative biology 56%, electrical engineering 51%, economics & finance 47%… mathematics lowest at just 0.7%. They honestly list limitations: each field's control is only 200 papers, so the per-field floor is coarse; math's low value is hard to interpret (low adoption, or the detector failing on math). They use v1 PDFs, score the body not the abstract (abstracts understate), and attach a bootstrap 95% CI to every figure.
items.why: 把它挑进来不是为了那个 32%，是为了那条方法纪律，正好接住昨天“任何提效说法先自己量一个真数”的线，并往前补了关键一环：光量还不够，得先钉住误报地板，否则你量出来的可能是工具自己的噪声在冒充趋势。对做 AI 产品和增长、天天要跟“AI 占比/命中率/贡献度”这类指标打交道的人，这是可直接抄的护身招式。三版行动就把它落成一条今晚能用的规矩：任何“几成是 AI”的数字，先要它的误报地板再决定信不信。
items.why_en: It's picked not for the 32% but for the method discipline, which catches yesterday's thread (“attach a real number to any efficiency claim”) and adds the missing piece: measuring isn't enough — you first have to pin the false-positive floor, or what you measured may be the tool's own noise masquerading as a trend. For anyone in AI product and growth who deals daily with “AI share / hit-rate / contribution” metrics, this is a directly copyable defensive move. Action 3 turns it into a rule you can use tonight: for any “N% is AI” number, get its false-positive floor before deciding whether to believe it.

items.title: 逆向工程现在很便宜了
items.author: Simon Willison
items.summary: 一条短笔记，点的却是个真变化。Simon Willison 说他不断听到有人用编程 agent 去逆向、自动化家里的设备。在 agent 之前，逆向一个没文档的设备并不是做不到，卡点一直是投入产出比：值不值得费这劲；更要命的是，这种不稳定、没文档的接口以后很可能变或坏，为它绑上一段没完没了的维护，划算吗。编程 agent 把这道账整个改了：让一个简单自动化跑起来的力气变小了，试错失败的成本也变小了；既然代码这么便宜，以后要改、甚至推倒重来的心理包袱就轻多了。
items.summary_en: A short note that points at a real change. Simon Willison says he keeps hearing about people using coding agents to reverse-engineer and automate devices in their homes. Before agents, reverse-engineering an undocumented device was entirely possible; the sticking point was ROI — was it worth the effort — and worse, an unstable, undocumented interface like that will likely change or break later, so committing to an endless maintenance cycle rarely paid off. Coding agents change that calculation entirely: the effort to get a simple automation working has dropped, as has the cost of trying and failing; and since the code is so cheap, the psychological baggage of having to change it later, or throw it away and start over, is far lighter.
items.why: 别被它的短骗了，它给今天的主线补了一个很实用的推论：当写代码和试错都变便宜，值得做的事情范围本身在扩张——以前因为 ROI 不够而放弃的一整类小自动化，现在都进了“值得做”的圈。它和一版那条 WordPress RCE 是同一趋势的两处印证：AI 把理解和改动代码的成本压到很低，一面是攻击的门槛塌了，一面是你亲手改造身边系统的门槛也塌了。今日上手就把它变成今晚一次亲手实验：挑一件以前嫌不值的琐事，让 agent 帮你逆向自动化掉。
items.why_en: Don't let its brevity fool you — it adds a practical corollary to today's through-line: when writing code and trying-and-failing both get cheap, the set of things worth doing itself expands, and a whole class of small automations you'd abandoned on ROI grounds now moves inside “worth doing.” It's a second reading of the same trend as Action 1's WordPress RCE: AI drives the cost of understanding and changing code so low that on one side the bar to attack collapses, and on the other the bar to reshape the systems around you with your own hands collapses too. 今日上手 turns it into a hands-on experiment tonight: pick a chore you'd deemed not worth it and have an agent reverse-engineer it into automation.

items.title: 翻出来的旧邮件：Altman 眼里，开源是一步棋不是礼物
items.title_en: A resurfaced email: to Altman, open source was a move, not a gift
items.author: Simon Willison
items.flag: ⚠️ 系引述早年内部邮件（诉讼公开材料流出的旧文），反映的是当时的战略措辞，未必等于今日 OpenAI 的立场；当历史注脚读，别当最新表态。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ This quotes an early internal email (an older document surfaced via litigation disclosures); it reflects the strategic wording of that time, not necessarily OpenAI's stance today. Read it as a historical footnote, not a current position.
items.summary: Simon Willison 摘引了一段早年的 Sam Altman 内部邮件。大意是：OpenAI 在讨论开源策略，想尽快放出一个能力约等于 GPT-3、能在消费级硬件上跑的语言模型，而且要抢在 Stability 或别人之前放。理由说得很直白——这么做“有助于打消别人发布同等能力模型的念头，也让新入场者更难拿到融资”。也就是说，开源在这套算盘里不是姿态，是一步用来压制竞争、抬高对手门槛的棋。
items.summary_en: Simon Willison quotes an early internal email from Sam Altman. The gist: OpenAI was discussing open-source strategy and wanted to soon release a language model with roughly GPT-3-level capability that could run on consumer hardware — and to do it before Stability or someone else did. The reasoning is blunt: doing so “helps discourage others from releasing similarly-powerful models, and makes it harder for new efforts to get funded.” In other words, open-sourcing here isn't a posture, it's a move to suppress competition and raise rivals' barriers.
items.why: 本报把它挑进来，是因为它从反面印证了今天的主线：真正起作用的从不是权重本身，而是谁把开源这步棋走进了自己的生态安排里。这周满屏“中国开源权重在赢”的读法，配上这段旧邮件正好互为镜子——开源可以是抬高对手门槛的攻，也可以是别人绑不住你的守，关键看它嵌在谁的盘子里。对靠这些模型搭产品的人，别把任何一方的“开源”当纯粹的善意或纯粹的威胁，当成一步随局势会变的棋来盘。带 flag 读：这是早年邮件，非今日表态。
items.why_en: This paper picks it because it confirms today's through-line from the other side: what works is never the weights themselves but who works the open-source move into their own ecosystem's arrangement. This week's wall-to-wall “Chinese open weights are winning” reading and this old email mirror each other — open source can be an offense that raises rivals' barriers or a defense that keeps you un-lockable, depending on whose board it sits on. For anyone building on these models, treat neither side's “open source” as pure goodwill or pure threat, but as a move that shifts with the game. Read it with the flag: an early email, not a current position.
